subject: FintechCo privacy/telemetry follow-up & action items
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@fintechco.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 15:32:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + ask: telemetry, retention windows, and subprocessor visibility

Hi Priya —

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation and we appreciate you walking us through FintechCo's production constraints. Quick recap so we're all aligned and to capture the follow-ups we promised: 

1) Data classification and PII: You confirmed that any customer-facing prompts that include account identifiers or transaction IDs are treated as high-sensitivity PII and must not be retained beyond the session window. You also noted a few edge cases where sanitized tokens can be stored for analytics.

2) Retention & logs: FintechCo requires request/response logs to be retained for 30 days for fraud investigations, then purged. Audit logs for key management & admin actions must be kept for 1 year.

3) Telemetry / third-party vendors: You asked for a list of telemetry vendors that might receive aggregated usage metrics (e.g., metrics collectors, error reporting). You also asked about any marketplace flows that could surface usage to cloud partners.

4) Subprocessor evidence: You requested high-level artifacts (SOC 2, subprocessor matrix) and a short explanation of which subprocessors see unredacted request content vs. aggregated telemetry.

Action items (owners and ETA):
- Soojin: Send the subprocessor matrix + the finite answers to which subprocessors may see unredacted content (ETA Thu, Jun 11).
- Monica: Provide the technical mapping for how we can enforce the 30-day request log purge and the 1-year admin audit retention (ETA Thu, Jun 11).
- Connor: Draft a proposed DPA clause for telemetry/exclusion and document our marketplace data flow (ETA Fri, Jun 12).

I attached the tracker workbook you shared during the call and a current copy of our subprocessor matrix for reference. If anything above is incorrect or missing, please flag. Once we close these items we can get legal to work the DPA language and schedule a short follow-up with your security team.

Best,

--
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@fintechco.com>

Cc: Data Privacy Ops <dpo@fintechco.com>, Ravi Menon <ravi.menon@fintechco.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 09:16:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap + ask: telemetry, retention windows, and subprocessor visibility

Thanks, Soojin — this captures the call well. A couple clarifications from the privacy/ops side: 

- When we say "unredacted request content," we mean raw user-provided text that contains PII. Aggregated telemetry (error counts, token-level latency) is acceptable to share with external vendors only if it cannot be re-identified to a user or account.
- For the 30-day request log retention, we need an automatic purge process and an API or audit record that shows deletion was performed (we prefer immutable delete events).
- Marketplace flows: our concern is any cloud marketplace where a partner could access billing/usage exports that contain request-level metadata. Please call out if any of your cloud partners (AWS/GCP/Azure marketplace) have visibility into request-level payloads in egress logs.

Also: please confirm whether any telemetry agent (e.g., Sentry, Datadog, internal metrics proxies) ever receives full request bodies or only metadata.

We attached a short questionnaire (filled by our GRC team) — we've included it in the workbook you sent. We'll expect the matrix and the technical mapping before we route this to our legal.

Thanks — Priya

--
Priya Shah
Head, Data Privacy Ops
FintechCo
priya.shah@fintechco.com | +1 (650) 555-0911

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@fintechco.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 13:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap + ask: telemetry, retention windows, and subprocessor visibility

Hi Priya —

Quick technical notes attached and a short mapping below. I also attached our current subprocessor matrix (redwood-subprocessor-matrix.pdf). High level: 

- What we store: By default, Redwood does not persist raw request bodies to long-term storage for hosted inference. For customers that enable request logging (for troubleshooting), logs are kept in a short-term log store by default and subject to the customer's retention policy. We support automatic TTL-based purges — we can configure a 30-day purge for your account.

- Telemetry vendors: Our analytics pipeline sends aggregated metrics (token counts, error rates, timing histograms) to internal telemetry. We push aggregated metrics to Datadog and an internal Redshift-based analytics cluster. Neither receives identifiable request body content in normal operation. The only exception is if a customer opts into debug-mode request dumps for a short window; those are gated, encrypted, and have a separate approval flow.

- Marketplace/cloud provider exposures: Marketplace billing records contain usage aggregates and billing metrics. They do not contain raw request payloads. Cloud provider control plane logs (e.g., GCP stackdriver or AWS CloudTrail) may capture API call metadata (timestamps, instance IDs) but not the request text. We will include a short note in the matrix clarifying this.

- Deletion/audit evidence: We can provide a deletion audit event stream (signed timestamps) showing TTL enforcement. We will outline the implementation in the attached doc.

Open items for us: 
- Confirm whether FintechCo wants a hard delete (crypto-shred) vs. logical deletion for the 30-day purge (we can support either within our private deployments, hosted flows require separate coordination).
- Confirm which cloud regions you require for data residency (us-east-1 only, or multi-region within US?).

I'll follow up with the exact wording we recommend for the DPA telemetry exclusion clause.

Best,
Monica
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0228
